explanation: The treaty is usually read for what it gave Portugal in the west. Read for what it left in the east it is the other half of the same fact: everything on the African side of the meridian stayed Portuguese, the Guinea and Angola coasts included. One crown therefore held both ends of a traffic that had not begun yet — the ports the captives were embarked at and the coast they were landed on. Wikipedia’s account of the Brazilian trade has most of the five and a half million embarking at West Central African ports, above all Luanda; that they were Portuguese ports is what 1494 settled.
